definitions.title: Double Integral in Polar Coordinates
definitions.latex: \iint_R f(x, y) \, dA = \int_\alpha^\beta \int_{r_1(\theta)}^{r_2(\theta)} f(r\cos\theta, r\sin\theta) \, r \, dr \, d\theta
definitions.statement: In polar coordinates, the differential area element is dA = r dr dtheta. The extra factor of r represents the Jacobian determinant of the transformation x = r cos(theta), y = r sin(theta).
definitions.explanation: A polar rectangle has radial length dr and arc length r dtheta, giving area r dr dtheta.
definitions.keyTakeaway: Always include the radial factor r in the polar area element: dA = r dr dtheta.

definitions.title: Gaussian Integral via Polar Double Integration
definitions.statement: Squaring the single-variable improper integral and converting to polar coordinates over the entire plane transforms the intractable integrand e^(-x^2) into the easily integrable form r e^(-r^2).
definitions.explanation: Produces I^2 = int_0^(2pi) int_0^oo e^(-r^2) r dr dtheta = pi, yielding I = sqrt(pi).
definitions.keyTakeaway: Classic demonstration of simplifying higher-dimensional integrals via polar symmetry.
